To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there are a lot of different retransmission-based transport protocols, (2) these protocols can be classified according to their reliability service and error control scheme and (3) the majority of protocols use a single error control scheme, namely the selective repeat ARQ scheme

1) the reliability services offered by the protocols can be categorized into three classes: (i) the service offered by TCP; (ii) the service offered UDP; and (iii) services in between; 2) the error control schemes employed by the protocols can also be categorized into three groups: (i) a scheme that is a variant of TCP; (ii)a scheme that is a hybrid of TCP and UDP; and (ii) a scheme that uses a different approach than TCP
the reliability services offered by retransmission-based protocols can be classified into four groups and that the error control schemes can be classified into three groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of transport protocols and with their implementation in real-time systems.
the classification of retransmissionbased partially reliable transport protocols with respect to their reliability service and error control scheme.
the design, analysis and evaluation of partially reliable transport services.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the majority of the existing retransmissionbased partially reliable transport protocols offer a reliability service that is a combination of the reliability services of UDP and TCP, and that the error control schemes of these protocols are either a combination of the error control schemes offered by UDP and TCP, or a modification or an extension of one of them.
the retransmission-based subclass of partially reliable protocols is very large and diverse.
the majority of existing protocols are either not fully specified or do not provide a reliable service.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided a unified terminology for the class of retransmission- based, partially reliable transport protocol, and we have shown that this terminology is sufficiently rich to describe all existing retransmissionbased, partially reliable transport protocls.
we provide a framework for the classification, analysis and comparison of partially reliable transport protocol, which is a class of protocols that has been neglected by researchers so far.

the taxonomy and the survey provide an overview and a reference point for the class of retransmission based, partially reliable transport protocol, and thus, they provide an important step in understanding and comparing these protocols.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is no single best partially reliable transport protocol, but rather that there exists a large variety of protocols that offer different reliability services and use different error control schemes, and that these protocols are suitable in different environments and applications.
a large variety of reliability services can be provided by retransmission-based protocols.

, in order to achieve a better understanding of the retransmission-based error control schemes employed by partially reliable transport protocols and thereby to gain insight into the performance of these protocols, it is essential to examine these protocols in the context of the reliability service they are designed to support.
